text:
maya (Support): Heads-up — after pushing the new rate-cap policy (canary, 5%) we got a spike in 429 reports from a handful of customers and an increase in tail latency. Opening a quick triage thread.

sam (Eng-Platform): Thanks. Which canary ID and what changed in the policy?

maya (Support): Canary id: canary-20260311-rc3. Policy diff attached from release notes:
```
- per_min: 600
+ per_min: 300
- short_burst_window: 30s
+ short_burst_window: 10s
- allow_burst_overage: true
+ burst_smoothing: enabled
```
Some customers with chat-heavy usage see repeated 429s within seconds.

liam (Eng-SRE): :eyes: Two quick asks: 1) can we get the token-bucket and prefix-cache hit metrics for canary-20260311-rc3? 2) are these customers hitting concurrent connection limits or token quota?

support-bot: Alert -> 2026-03-11T14:20Z: rate_limit_429_rate increased to 8% (baseline 0.3%) for canary-20260311-rc3. Top-affected customers: acme-inc, hyperchat, docsly. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rl/canary-20260311-rc3

nina (Oncall): Can we get a repro script so CS can throttle or advise customers? If we need to rollback, what's the rollback playbook?

maya (Support): Repro curl (triggers 429 within ~20s on affected tenant):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"open-gpt","input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\n  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```

sam (Eng-Platform): Confirmed: the new short_burst_window reduction + lower per_min reduced smoothing. Canary config accidentally applied to both rate and quota buckets. We should: 1) immediately pause further canary ramp, 2) scale canary back to 0% (stop traffic routing to canary), 3) consider rolling back to canary-20260310 baseline.

deploy-bot: Received rollback request. Command to run: `infra deploy config:apply --target=canary-20260311-rc3 --revert-to=canary-20260310 --reason="429 spike" --approve`

liam (Eng-SRE): Before full revert, quick mitigations we can try in place: - revert short_burst_window to 30s (manual patch) - enable per-tenant backpressure bypass for known customers for 1 hour - increase token bucket refill rate by 20% for canary traffic. Which is fastest?

sam (Eng-Platform): Fastest is manual patch to short_burst_window -> 30s. I'll prepare a patch and request deploy-bot. If that doesn't reduce 429s in 10m, we revert to previous canary.

maya (Support): I'll notify affected customers and give the repro script + recommended retry/backoff (exponential with jitter). Also collecting logs and customer request IDs.

nina (Oncall): I'll watch the dashboards and set an alert for 429 > 1% for the canary after the patch. If it stays >1% for 15m, escalate to rollback.

support-bot: Ticket created: S-2026-1453 linking acme-inc/hyperchat/docsly. Assigning to maya.

sam (Eng-Platform): Patch prepared and staged. Pushing now.

deploy-bot: Patch applied to canary-20260311-rc3: short_burst_window=30s. Metric recompute triggered.

liam (Eng-SRE): Early signal: 429 dropped from 8% -> 1.2% in 4m, latency tail improving. Continue monitoring for 15m.

maya (Support): Customer updates sent. They're testing their clients with the repro script. They report immediate improvement.

nina (Oncall): 15m passed, metrics stable at ~0.9% 429. Closing immediate escalation. Next steps: postmortem and adjust rollout checklist.

sam (Eng-Platform): Agreed. Action items: - roll out canary rule change to only modify per_min in staged steps (50% increments) - add automated canary rollback threshold check (429 > 1% for 5m) - add a preflight that simulates bursty traffic for the target percent of users.

liam (Eng-SRE): I'll own the canary guardrails ticket and include the token-bucket telemetry we needed.

maya (Support): Thanks team. I'll close the customer tickets once final verification done. :white_check_mark:
